source_name: Cutting Tool Wear Audio Dataset (Kaggle, nachiketsoni)
citation: N. Soni, A. Kumar and H. Patel, Acoustic Analysis of Cutting Tool Vibrations of Machines for Anomaly Detection and Predictive Maintenance, IEEE R10-HTC 2023, doi:10.1109/R10-HTC57504.2023.10461855

label_rules.rationale: Dataset description: 'base machine sound files' = machine running without cutting.
Folder FRESH = sharp tool cutting; treated as stable normal cutting.
Moderately blunt tool while the cut itself is acceptable: MSM label 2 (tool defect, cutting normal). Decision by project owner, 2026-10-14.

Listening review: cutting continued after the tool broke, which should have been stopped: MSM label 1. Breakage onset to be marked as an interval label from the spectrogram review. Decision by project owner, 2026-10-14.

fields.evidence: File names RPM520... / RPM635...; description: 'at 2 different RPMs - 520 and 635'.
Description: 'end-mill cutters with a diameter of 16mm'.
Description: 'The workpiece used was of mild-steel'.
The letter in the file name (A/B/C) encodes the wear state, so it would leak the label; kept in provenance only.

unresolved: Breakage onset is an expert estimate from one recording (BROKEN520 C0005, 1.0-1.55 s); a listening check by the project owner is recommended. An earlier high-frequency burst at C0004 0.5-3 s may be a precursor (chip or crack); kept as label 2.

BROKEN635 shows no breakage event: assumed cut with the already broken tool (label 1 throughout). Hypothesis, NOT applied: C0001-C0012 may have run at 520 rpm (envelope peak 8.7 Hz vs 10.5 Hz from C0013). Blind test 2026-10-14 (verification/2026-10-14_band_claims) showed the envelope peak is not a reliable rpm estimator on MSM, so N keeps the file-name value until harmonic/tooth-pass checks confirm it.
Microphone type and position are not stated; mic_type kept 'unknown'.
Machine model, feed, depth and width of cut are not stated.

interval_labels.evidence: Spectrogram review 2026-10-14: recording before the breakage onset in RPM520C0005 (envelope dominated by 17 Hz = 2x rev). Tool worn but cut continuing: label 2 per project owner.

Spectrogram review 2026-10-14 (proto/scripts/ctwa_zoom.py, 50 ms frames): energy above 4 kHz falls 25 dB from 1.0 s to 1.45 s, broadband transient at 1.52 s; afterwards 50-600 Hz stays ~18 dB lower and later recordings switch to a once-per-revolution (8.7 Hz) envelope with impact harmonics (C0007). Rest of the file and all later BROKEN files keep the file-level label 1.
